comments.title: Meters lack direct line-of-sight to serving transformer pads
comments.comment: Building structures obstruct the visual path from transformer pads to many exterior meter locations, and no written Austin Energy approval has been provided for non-line-of-sight configurations.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires each transformer to be within unobstructed line of sight of its serving meter(s) so AE personnel can verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations. The following deficiencies are present:
- Meters distributed on the east, west, and south faces of buildings are on the opposite side from their likely source transformer, with the building structure physically blocking the sightline
- No documentation (sight-line diagram, building section, or 3D analysis) confirms an unobstructed visual path from any transformer pad to its associated meters
- No written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing non-line-of-sight meter placements has been provided
- The routing distance from the western transformer pad to Building 3 meters is estimated at over 150 feet, potentially exceeding operational practice standards for the 'within sight' requirement
- Building elevations confirming all meters are on the first floor or ground level have not been submitted
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.applicableArea: Transformer pads and corresponding meter locations for Buildings 1–8 throughout the site; specifically meter locations on east, west, and south building faces; western transformer pad to Building 3 routing (~150+ ft estimated)
comments.resolution: Provide one of the following: (1) Relocate all meters to building faces with a direct, unobstructed line of sight to their serving transformer pad, and submit building elevations or a sight-line diagram on Sheet 21 confirming each meter is on the first floor or ground level and within unobstructed view of its transformer; OR (2) Submit documented written approval from both Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing each non-line-of-sight meter location. Additionally, address the western transformer-to-Building 3 routing distance: if the direct line-of-sight distance exceeds 150 feet, confirm whether AE accepts this configuration or reposition the transformer or meters accordingly.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: EL-14.39 (1/3 runs) flagged a possible >150-ft routing distance from the western transformer to Building 3 meters — reviewer should confirm whether this operational practice distance threshold applies and whether it affects the line-of-sight determination.

perRunFindings.comment: Direct line of sight from transformers to meters not verified. Provide line of sight analysis or building sections confirming unobstructed visual path from each transformer pad to its corresponding meter location(s), or provide documented AE Design approval for exceptions.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations and corresponding meter locations

perRunFindings.comment: Many meter locations on building faces do not have direct unobstructed line of sight to transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Meters on the east/west/south sides of buildings cannot see transformers on opposite sides. Provide: (1) Confirmation that all meters are relocated to faces that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer, OR (2) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing the non-line-of-sight meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple buildings and meter locations throughout site

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer pads not in direct line of sight to meter location. Buildings and trees block visual path from transformer pad to meters.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads to associated meters on Buildings 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8

perRunFindings.comment: Provide building elevations and a site plan diagram showing sight lines between all electrical meters and their serving transformers, confirming that: (1) meters are located on first floor or ground level, and (2) unobstructed sight line exists from transformer to meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.

Electrical meters are shown on building exterior walls (Sheet 21), but no documentation is provided confirming that each meter is located on the first floor or ground level and within line-of-sight of its corresponding transformer. Provide notes or details on the electrical plan documenting the meter height and sight line relationship to each transformer.
applicableAreas: Building exterior walls where electrical meters are mounted in relation to transformer pad locations

perRunFindings.comment: Many meter locations shown on Sheet 21 are not within sight of transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Provide: (1) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design AND Distribution Metering business units authorizing meter locations without direct line of sight to transformers, OR (2) Reposition all meters to locations that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer on first floor/ground level per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
applicableAreas: Multiple meter locations throughout the site

perRunFindings.comment: Transformer to meter line of sight distance may be excessive. Routing from western transformer pad to Building 3 appears to exceed 150 feet, potentially exceeding operational practice standards for 'within sight' requirement.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to distant meters

comments.title: Service disconnects absent from plans; meter and disconnect labels incomplete
comments.comment: No service disconnect locations are shown anywhere in the plan set, meters lack individual identifying labels, and no meter schedule or specification table has been provided.
comments.issue:
UCM §§ 1.9.3.1 and 1.16.0 require plans to show and label both meters and their associated disconnects, confirm grouping, and demonstrate that the distance between each meter and its disconnect does not exceed 20 feet with line-of-sight maintained. The following are missing:
- Disconnect locations not shown on Sheet 21 (electrical plan) or on Sheets 9, 19, or 31 (site, wet utilities, landscape plans)
- All 8 meters are labeled generically as 'Electrical Meters' with no unique identifiers (e.g., M-1 through M-8); pull boxes are labeled generically as 'Electrical Pull Box' with no individual IDs (e.g., PB-1, PB-2)
- No meter schedule or specification table identifying meter ID, building served, type (single-phase/three-phase), and location
- Distance between each meter and its corresponding disconnect not indicated; compliance with the 20-foot maximum and line-of-sight requirement (UCM § 1.9.3.1.J) cannot be verified
- No service distribution enclosure (SDE) or wireway locations labeled for grouped metering configurations
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All 8 meter locations and associated service disconnects for Buildings 1–8 throughout the site
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21: (1) show and label all service disconnect locations; (2) assign unique identifiers to each meter (M-1 through M-8, corresponding to Buildings 1–8) and each pull box (PB-1, PB-2, etc.); (3) add a meter schedule or specification table showing meter ID, building served, type, and location; (4) dimension the distance between each meter and its disconnect (maximum 20 ft) and annotate the line-of-sight relationship per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J; (5) label any service distribution enclosure or wireway locations. Add meter and disconnect callout labels to Sheets 9, 19, and 31 as well.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: 15:EL-15.32 (1/3 runs) specifically flagged the need for unique meter and pull box IDs — reviewer should confirm whether a formal meter schedule is required at this stage of review.

perRunFindings.comment: Show and label all service disconnects on the electrical plan. Indicate their location relative to meters (grouped together per code requirements) and verify they are within 20 feet and line of sight of the meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J.

Meters and disconnects not labeled on all required sheets. Label all electrical meters and disconnects on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. For grouped metering, label the service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway location, and note the distance between meters and disconnects (maximum 20 feet, must be within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Specify meter specifications (single-phase, three-phase, main vs. sub-meter).

Individual labels are required for all meters and disconnects. Assign unique identifiers to each of the 8 meters (e.g., 'M-1' through 'M-8' corresponding to Buildings 1-8) and to all pull boxes (e.g., 'PB-1', 'PB-2', etc.). Show these labels clearly on Sheet 21 and on all other plan sheets where meters appear. Create a meter schedule or specification table on the electrical plan showing meter identification, building served, location, and type.

Provide building electrical plans, riser diagrams, or service disconnect location drawings showing the distance between electrical meters and their serving main service disconnects, confirming distance does not exceed 20 feet and that meter and disconnect are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.

comments.title: Meter placement compliance with prohibited locations not documented
comments.comment: No documentation confirms that the eight exterior meter locations comply with UCM § 1.9.3.1 restrictions on prohibited placements, gas meter separation, or flood elevation requirements.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.9.3.1 prohibits meters from being located on or under porches, stairways, overhangs exceeding 72 inches, or carports, and requires a minimum 3-foot separation from gas meters/regulators/relief valves and installation at least 1 foot above the 100-year flood elevation. Sheet 21 shows meters on building exterior walls but provides no architectural elevations, detail sections, or plan notations demonstrating: (1) meters are not beneath prohibited features (porches, stairways, overhangs >72 in., carports); (2) a minimum 3-foot separation from any gas meters or regulators is maintained; (3) meters meet the 1-foot-above-100-year-flood-elevation requirement (the site is in FEMA Zone X, but no flood elevation documentation for meter mounting heights has been provided).
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9)
comments.resolution: Provide building elevations or meter location detail sheets for each building showing: (1) the meter position relative to porches, overhangs, stairways, and carports, with confirmation that no meter is beneath a prohibited feature or under an overhang exceeding 72 inches; (2) gas meter locations (if present) with a dimension confirming at least 3-foot separation from electrical meters; (3) a note or grading plan reference confirming meter mounting heights are at least 1 foot above the 100-year flood elevation (a general note referencing the FEMA Zone X classification with a stated mounting height is acceptable).
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs each for EL-3.39 and EL-10.61) — reviewer should confirm whether building elevations exist elsewhere in the submittal and whether architectural detail is required at this stage.

perRunFindings.comment: Building elevations or meter location detail sheets must be provided showing that electrical meters are NOT located on/under porches, stairways, overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or other prohibited locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1. Provide building elevations with meter locations clearly identified relative to architectural features.

Meter location compliance with prohibited locations and flood elevation requirements is not demonstrated. Please provide: (1) architectural elevations showing meter locations relative to building porch/stairway/overhang obstructions; (2) 3-foot separation verification from gas meters (show gas meter locations if present); (3) elevation certificates or grading plan showing meters are minimum 1 foot above 100-year flood level (or FEMA determination if in floodplain); (4) notes confirming meters are readily accessible and on first floor/ground level within sight of transformer.

comments.title: Electrical routing from Valley View Road ROW not confirmed on private property
comments.comment: The underground electrical line is shown entering the site from Valley View Road public right-of-way, and the plans do not confirm that all routing from the utility connection point onward is located entirely on private property.
comments.issue: UCM §§ 1.10.4 and 1.9.3.1 require electrical routing from the initial public utility connection point through transformers to meters to be located entirely on private property. Sheet 21 labels the incoming line as 'Underground Electric Line' where it enters from Valley View Road (public ROW). Property line boundaries are not clearly marked along the full routing path, so compliance with the 100% private-property routing requirement cannot be confirmed from the submitted plans.
comments.applicableArea: Electrical routing from Valley View Road ROW entry point through transformer pads and meter locations
comments.resolution: On Sheet 21, clearly delineate property line boundaries along the full electrical routing path and annotate or note that all underground electrical routing from the utility connection point is within private property or an established private easement. If any segment routes within public ROW or a public easement, provide documentation of applicable permits, franchise agreements, or easement authorizations.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Resolution may involve coordination with Austin Energy and Public Works / ROW Management if any routing segment falls within Valley View Road public right-of-way.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs) — reviewer should confirm whether the Valley View Road entry point shown on Sheet 21 is a standard AE service point within an established easement or a genuine private-property routing compliance gap.

perRunFindings.comment: Electrical routing from public utility connection point to transformer and meters not verified as 100% on private property. Provide routing diagram or plan notes clearly indicating property line boundaries and confirming that all electrical routing from the initial public utility connection point through transformers to all meters is located entirely on private property and does not route through public ROW or public easements.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from public ROW entry point through transformer and meter locations
